yt_posts.topic: The real track record, the ElizaOS lawsuit lesson, and the Robinhood chain hunt
yt_posts.engagement_question: Which of my old calls surprised you the most when you saw the multiplier?
yt_posts.body:
Let me actually show you the receipts, because I get a lot of "is this guy for real" energy from people who just found the channel.

LAB: called it in October off an insider alert, we bottomed together in December around 7.8 cents, and by June it had run to a 353x. Farcoin: I thought the name was kind of dumb when the alert first hit, and it still did an 86x. NYX: called in May last year, took a few months to explode into a 550x by September. Tutorial on BNB: 94x back in September, then made a fresh all-time high again just last week for another leg to 127x. Pippin: 85x, called in the middle of a bear market when nobody wanted to hear it. Velvet: 58x over eleven months, retraced hard, and is pumping again right now. Giggle Fun: 30x even though one wallet held 80 percent of the supply when we called it. Russell: 12x off a dog-on-Coinbase listing in March.

None of that is luck. It's volume: if you put a thousand dollars into ten different calls and five go to zero, the other five, especially the one that does 900x, more than cover the losses. That's the actual math behind every "how are you always finding these" comment I get.

Here's the flip side, because I want you to see the risk too, not just the wins. ElizaOS was the third largest AI token in existence behind TAO and Virtuals during the entire Trump-pump run. It had every quality you'd want: real exchange listings, a serious founder, actual usage. Then the founder got hit with a lawsuit he couldn't afford to fight, and the token has done nothing but go down since. Great fundamentals do not protect you from a courtroom. I had members in that one because of me, and I lost out on it too. That's crypto. You take the risk with your eyes open.

Right now the hunt is on the Robinhood chain. Cooper, a real office dog at the Robinhood HQ, is my top pick, with major marketing starting this week off a 54k low. Cash Cat was about to get flipped by a louder, more vocal community called $IF, and then, out of nowhere, got listed directly on the Robinhood app the same week. Make of that timing what you want. Same game as LAB and Farcoin: most of these go nowhere, and the ones that don't pay for all of it.
